format_coverage: The real AI-901 exam draws from Microsoft's full item-type repertoire: multiple choice, multi-part/multi-select questions, build list (ordering), drag and drop, hot area, active screen, case studies, and problem-solution sets. Microsoft does not publish which of these appear on any given exam, and Microsoft Learn access is excluded from Fundamentals exams. This mock supports three formats and approximates as follows. Multiple choice maps exactly to single_choice. Multi-part and multi-select items map to multiple_response - but this mock scores them all-or-nothing, while Microsoft awards one point per correctly answered component, so this mock's multi-response scoring is STRICTER than the real exam's. Drag and drop is approximated by scenario_matching: mapping scenarios onto a reused option set exercises the same discrimination without the same interaction. Build list, hot area, active screen, case studies and problem-solution sets are NOT rehearsed at all - a candidate would meet those interactions for the first time in the real exam. This matters more for AI-901 than for a describe-level fundamentals exam: 55-60% of AI-901's weight is on IMPLEMENTING solutions in Microsoft Foundry - work whose real assessment involves portal screens, SDK code and CLI invocations - so a text-only mock necessarily tests recognition of the right implementation move rather than performance of it. Format shares here are a documented default rather than observed calibration: the official practice assessment is behind a sign-in wall and was not accessed, and the one accessible community practice source is 81% four-option single choice with 12% of its items in forms this player cannot render. Finally, the real exam mixes unidentified unscored pilot items into the paper and reports a scaled 1-1,000 score with a 700 pass mark that Microsoft states may not equal 70% of the points, so no raw percentage from this mock converts to a Microsoft score.
